record.paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
record.original_question: Determine whether Brownian motion can be characterized by functional equations, in the same spirit that several singular or nowhere differentiable functions can be characterized as unique solutions of simultaneous functional equations.

evidence.quote: C. Sempi [230] asked whether it is possible to characterize the Brownian motion via functional equations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Several classical singular or nowhere-differentiable functions (for example, Cantor's staircase, the Takagi function, de Rham's curves, and certain self-affine functions) admit a characterization as the unique bounded (or otherwise suitably constrained) solution of a system of simultaneous functional equations of the form
  f(φ_i(x)) = a_i f(x) + b_i(x),  i = 1,…,k,
where {φ_i} are given contractions covering the domain and the data (a_i, b_i) determine f uniquely.

Standard one-dimensional Brownian motion is the unique (in law) real-valued stochastic process {B(t) : t ≥ 0} with B(0) = 0, almost surely continuous sample paths, independent increments, and B(t) − B(s) ∼ N(0, t − s) for 0 ≤ s ≤ t.

Problem. Determine whether Brownian motion can be characterized as the unique solution (in an appropriate function/process space, with suitable regularity or distributional constraints) of a system of simultaneous functional equations, analogous to the functional-equation characterizations available for classical singular and nowhere-differentiable functions. Either exhibit such a system of functional equations whose unique solution is Brownian motion (specifying the solution space and the sense of uniqueness), or prove that no such characterization is possible.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of the question of characterizing Brownian motion via simultaneous functional equations in the spirit of characterizations of singular/nowhere-differentiable functions. No clear solution or refutation was located, so the current status is unverified.

status_evidence.title: Brownian motion - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: General references describe Brownian motion via Gaussian/covariance properties, not as the unique solution of a system of functional equations.
status_evidence.claim: Standard characterizations of Brownian motion are distributional rather than via simultaneous functional equations.

status_evidence.title: Wiener process - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Wiener process is characterized by independent Gaussian increments and continuous paths.
status_evidence.claim: No functional-equation characterization analogous to that of singular functions is given in standard references.
